src: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
s: President Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh in 1973 because of:
x: Jai Andhra Movement President's Rule was imposed in Andhra Pradesh in 1973 following the Jai Andhra Movement, a separatist agitation in the Andhra region demanding a separate state. This followed widespread unrest and breakdown of normal administration. It was one of several instances of political turbulence in the state's history.

src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
s: The Jai Andhra Movement 1972-73 finally ended with
o: The arrest of many students and women leaders
The suppression by central reserved forces
The Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
x: The Jai Andhra Movement of 1972-73, an agitation from the Andhra region seeking separation, was ultimately resolved and ended following the Central Government's proposal of the ' Six-Point Formula '-a set of measures aimed at addressing regional grievances and preserving the unity of the state.

src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2019
s: How did the Jai Andhra Movement end in 1972–73?
o: With the abolition of Mulki Rules
With the arrests of many student and women leaders
As the Central forces suppressed the movement
With the Six-Point Formula proposed by the Central Government
x:
The Jai Andhra Movement (1972–73) emerged in the Andhra region in response to the implementation of the Mulki Rules, which gave preference to local candidates in public employment in Telangana. The movement demanded either the abolition of the Mulki Rules or the creation of a separate Andhra State. It witnessed widespread protests, demonstrations and political instability. To resolve the regional tensions, the Central Government introduced the Six-Point Formula in 1973. The formula aimed to ensure balanced regional development, provide equitable opportunities in education and employment, and reduce regional disparities. It eventually replaced the earlier safeguards and brought the movement to an end. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Jai Andhra Movement – 1972–73
• Ended with – Six-Point Formula (1973)
• Objective – Regional balance and employment safeguards

src: APPSC Group-II 2019
s: What was the main factor that led to the Jai Andhra Movement?
o: Supreme Court Judgment on Mulki Rules
Imposition of high taxes on Andhras
Problems in water supply between Andhra and Telangana regions
Giving less priority to Andhras in administration
x:
The immediate cause of the Jai Andhra Movement (1972) was the Supreme Court's judgment upholding the validity of the Mulki Rules, which provided preference in public employment to local candidates of the Telangana region. Many people in the Andhra region viewed the judgment as discriminatory, leading to widespread protests demanding either the abolition of the Mulki Rules or the creation of a separate Andhra State. The movement ultimately led to the Six-Point Formula (1973) as a political solution. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Immediate Cause – Supreme Court Judgment on Mulki Rules
• Movement – Jai Andhra (1972)

src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
s: What was the main factor leading to Jai Andhra Movement? pr
o: Least importance given to Andhras' in
Imposition of heavy taxes on Andhras
Supreme Court's judgment on Mulki rules
Problems in the distribution of water between
x: Supreme Court's judgment on Mulki rules The Supreme Court's judgment on the Mulki Rules was a major factor leading to the Jai Andhra Movement. The verdict was seen by many in Andhra as unfavourable to their interests within the united state. This triggered widespread protests demanding a separate Andhra state in 1972-73.

src: APPSC Group-II 2019
s: The Six-Point Formula came into force through this Constitutional Amendment?
x:
The Six-Point Formula, evolved in 1973 to resolve the regional issues arising from the Jai Andhra Movement and the Telangana Movement, was given constitutional protection through the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973. The amendment inserted Article 371D and Article 371E into the Constitution, enabling special provisions relating to public employment, education and administrative arrangements in Andhra Pradesh. Article 371D provided for equitable opportunities and facilities for people belonging to different regions of the State in matters of public employment and education. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Constitutional Amendment – 32nd Amendment Act, 1973
• Inserted – Articles 371D & 371E
• Purpose – Implementation of Six-Point Formula

src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
s: The Six Points Formula came into effect under the Constitutional Amendment of:
x: 32nd Amendment The Six Point Formula, aimed at addressing regional imbalances between Andhra and Telangana, came into effect under the 32nd Constitutional Amendment. This amendment gave constitutional backing to safeguards for Telangana's development and employment. It remained a key reference point in later Telangana-related political debates.

src: APPSC Group-II 2011
s: Who led the anti-alcohol and Swadeshi movements in Dattamandalas?
x:
Kallur Subbarao was one of the prominent nationalist leaders of Rayalaseema (Dattamandalas). He actively led the antiliquor (anti-arrack) campaign and promoted the Swadeshi Movement, encouraging the use of indigenous goods and the boycott of foreign products. He also participated in various phases of the Indian freedom struggle and contributed significantly to political awakening in Rayalaseema. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Anti-liquor & Swadeshi Movement in Dattamandalas
• Leader – Kallur Subbarao

src: APPSC Group-II Mains 2017
s: In which region in 1991 did women start the Anti-Arrack Movement?
x:
The Anti-Arrack Movement began in 1991 in Dubagunta village of Nellore district. The movement was led primarily by rural women, who protested against the widespread consumption of arrack because it resulted in domestic violence, indebtedness and poverty. The movement soon spread throughout Andhra Pradesh and ultimately influenced the State Government to impose prohibition on arrack. The movement is regarded as one of the most successful women-led social movements in India. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Movement Started – Dubagunta
• Year – 1991
• Nature – Women's Anti-Arrack Movement
